To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

highly porous Mn3O4 micro/nanoparticles with in situ formed porous carbon as anode material were prepared via a simple hydrothermal route and exhibited a high reversible specific capacity, good cycling stability, and high rate performance for lithium storage.

highly porous Mn3O4 micro/nanoparticles with in situ formed C are prepared via a facile one-pot method, exhibiting large reversible capacity and excellent rate and cycling stability as an anode material for LIBs.

we design and synthesize a novel hierarchical Mn3 O4 -C composite with in situ formed C matrix, which shows excellent cycling stability, rate performance, and high reversible specific capacity, which makes it a promising anode material for LIBs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and fabrication of hierarchical transition metal oxide/carbon composites for energy storage and conversion applications.
the design and synthesis of hierarchical porous Mn3 O 4 micro/nanoparticles and their application as advanced anode material for high-performance Li-ion batteries.
the design and synthesis of a highly porous Mn3O4 micro/nanobcuboid with in situ formed C matrix as a novel anode material for Li-ion batteries.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this study has demonstrated a facile and effective synthetic method to fabricate hierarchical transition metal oxide-carbon hybrids with controlled pore structure, which is expected to be a promising candidate for advanced anode materials for lithium-ion batteries.
the highly porous Mn3O4@C micro/nanocupoids are synthesized via a facile one-pot hydrotherma method.

the highly porous Mn3O4 micro/nanoboids with in situ coated carbon matrix exhibit excellent electrochemical performance as anode material in lithium-ion batteries, which can be further applied in the energy storage and conversion fields.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the highly porous Mn3O4 micro/nanocrystallites are synthesized by a facile one-pot hydro-thermal route with the assistance of glucose.
we have developed a simple and efficient synthetic strategy to fabricate hierarchical Mn3 O4 /carbon hybrids with controlled morphology and pore structure.
the highly porous structure of Mn3 O4 is beneficial to the formation of continuous carbon matrix with rich pores in the cuboid.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the in situ formed carbon with porous structure is a good choice for enhancing the electrochemical performance of the transition metal oxides, and it can be used as a promising candidate in energy storage and conversion devices.
the highly porous Mn3O4 micro/nanoparticles with carbon matrix are designed and fabricated via a one-pet hydrothermal method.

the hierarchical porous structure with in situ coated carbon matrix can not only effectively improve the electrical conductivity and ion transport, but also facilitate the accommodation of volume change during cycling, which are the key factors to achieve the superior electrochemical performance of transition metal oxides as anode materials for lithium-ion batteries.
